newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam coffee market quiet as world prices fall.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam coffee market quiet as world prices fall.

text.p: Vietnam's robusta coffee market was quiet on Friday following a slide in futures prices this week in London and New York from recent highs, dealers said.
Prices rose slightly in the internal market earlier in the week on active trading, but selling by farmers in the country's main producing area had declined since Wednesday, they said.

Late week export prices were around $1,340-50 per tonne FOB Saigon Port. Vietnam has exported an estimated 220,000 tonnes of coffee so far from its 1996/97 crop and dealers reckoned around 40,000 tonnes remained.

New York's CSCE futures tumbled on Thursday as commodity funds sold heavily on talk of a stock build-up caused by producers seeking to take advantage of prices which in early March reached their highest levels in 2-1/2 years.

Traders said technical signs in London indicated prices could fall by $170 on the opening but noted that they expected the magnitude of decline to be less severe, around $60-$100, with strong support likely to come in at the $1,515 level.
"It could be an ugly day for robusta," said one trader. "New York, though, is continuing to look unpredicatble."
Vietnam's coffee is harvested in October. Dealers expect around 30,000 tonnes to sell before the summer lull.
